results.title_en: Unlocking Senegal’s dairy potential: The role of improved feed and stabling practices
results.description_en:
Dairy demand in Senegal exceeds domestic supply, despite the country’s large cattle herd and significant potential to expand production. To realize this potential, however, challenges related to low productivity, seasonal fluctuations, and limited market linkages must be addressed.

This study analyzes the effects of introducing improved cowpea forage and sheltering practices on milk production and revenues among agropastoral producers in the Louga and Thiès regions, using quantitative simulations within a System Dynamics model. Results indicate that improved forage enhances milk output throughout the year, including during the dry season and sheltering can help improve it further.

However, it is important to note that the improve forage grown must cover the needs for the entire dry season, else the cost of purchased feed may outweigh the benefits in increased productivity. Improved market access is also essential for translating milk productivity gains into higher revenues, particularly in areas where marketing opportunities remain limited.

results.title: Farmer-centric bundled climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices restore degraded landscapes and ecosystems, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and enhance carbon sequestration, strengthening smallholder farmers' resilience and adaptive capacity.
results.description: The farmer-centric bundled climate-smart agriculture (CSA) approach emerged in response to widespread land degradation and the need for more resilient farming systems. Traditional practices often failed to address ecosystem decline, leaving communities vulnerable to climate-related risks, including increasing rainfall intensity and variability, water stress, soil erosion, deforestation, severe land degradation and fragmentation, declining soil fertility, shortage of livestock feed, and increased incidence of crop and livestock diseases and pests. To tackle these challenges, the CSA bundles integrate crop and livestock practices that restore degraded landscapes, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, enhance carbon sequestration, and strengthen smallholder farmers' resilience and adaptive capacity. The bundle includes integrated watershed management and landscape rehabilitation, cereal-legume rotation and intensification, community forestry, development of communal grazing lands through area closures, forage production, and agroforestry. By combining these practices on a scale, the CSA bundles provide end-to-end solutions for farmers and communities: improving soil fertility, increasing productivity, stabilizing ecosystems, and delivering climate and livelihood benefits across multiple landscapes.

results.title: Learning and adoption of climate-Smart technologies for a women-led cooperative society
results.description: From 2023 to 2024 AICCRA’s partnership with Kimatwa Women Savings and Credit Cooperative (SACCO) in Makueni, Kenya co-developed bundled solutions to boost resilience, by facilitating learning and adoption of CSA technologies. These technologies include “Rip 1, get 1 free ripping,” forecasts directly from Kenya Metrological Department, crop calendar discussions, three “levels” of demos – mother trials, baby trials, and farmer experimentation and zai pits. As a result, adoption rose by 30% and for the first time in seven years (in 2024), farmers had stable bean yields and improved harvests of maize, green grams, and cowpeas.

results.title: Smart production and soils bundled solution for smallholders in Northern Ghana
results.description: Climatic stresses in northern Ghana is contributing to declining soil fertility and increased vulnerability of crop production systems. In addition, continued reliance on conventional land preparation practices such as ploughing and harrowing has further degraded soil structure, making soils vulnerable to erosion, as well as loss of organic matter and beneficial microbes and fauna. The smart production and soils bundled solution is therefore deployed to enhance resilient production and soil health for maize and cowpea production systems in Northern Ghana. The bundled solution includes Seasonal forecast, nowcast, tillage options, sustainable mechanisation, roller planters and crop and site specific fertiliser type and application rate. This is disseminated through multiple channels including radio, sms, field demonstrations, credit access to small tools and fertilisers. This is being deployed via an inclusive business model involving multiple agri- SME's in a partnership.

results.title: A one health approach to prioritizing emerging zoonotic diseases (EZDs) in northern Vietnam
results.description: Background: Vietnam, with its significant agricultural sector, large livestock population, rich biodiversity and close human-animal interactions, is highly vulnerable to zoonotic disease transmission. To better address this threat, representatives from the human, animal, and environmental health sectors in Vietnam worked together at two one health zoonotic disease prioritization (OHZDP) workshops to develop a list of priority zoonotic diseases for multisectoral one health collaboration in Hoa Binh and Lao Cai provinces in April 2024. Methods: We modified the OHZDP process, developed by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and utilized it to prioritize zoonotic diseases in Vietnam. This involved conducting defining prioritization criteria, developing specific questions with assigned weights for each criterion, and organizing two workshops with stakeholders. Result: There were 25 participants in Hoa Binh's workshop (7 females and 18 males), and 27 participants in Lao Cai's workshop (9 females and 18 males). Following a discussion of tool outputs among experts, four zoonotic diseases were prioritized in Lao Cai province: Rabies, avian influenza, Streptococcus suis, and leptospirosis. In Hoa Binh province, three diseases were identified as priorities: Rabies, avian influenza, and Streptococcus suis. Conclusion: Rabies, avian influenza and Streptococcus suis were the three most prioritized diseases across the two provinces. This list can serve as a foundation for strengthening one health collaboration for disease prevention and control in these targeted provinces.

results.title: A Bundled Farmer-Centric Climate-Smart Agriculture System Integrating Crop–Livestock Practices for Landscape and Ecosystem Restoration
results.description: A bundled farmer-centric climate-smart agriculture (CSA) system that integrates complementary crop and livestock practices to restore degraded landscapes, strengthen ecosystem functions, and build resilience in mixed farming systems. Designed for application at both farm and landscape levels, the system combines integrated watershed management, landscape rehabilitation, cereal–legume rotations, community forestry, improved communal grazing through area closures, forage production, and agroforestry within a coherent and spatially aligned implementation framework. By sequencing and integrating these practices rather than applying them as standalone interventions, the approach addresses soil degradation, water stress, feed shortages, and climate risks simultaneously while improving soil fertility, productivity, and ecosystem stability. It provides an end-to-end, scalable solution that enhances adaptive capacity, supports carbon sequestration and sustainable land management, and delivers climate and livelihood benefits across diverse smallholder landscapes.

results.title: From data to decision: Institutionalizing smart fertilizer recommendations through HaFAS in Ethiopia
results.description: The NextGen Decision Support Tool (DST), the engine behind HaFAS, delivers climate-smart, site-specific fertilizer recommendations using machine learning and a rich data backbone that includes over 100,000 crop trials, 20,000 soil profiles, and high-resolution agro-climatic layers. This enables dynamic guidance on nutrient needs and agronomic practices, while linking to financial and risk-management services. By the end of 2024, the DST had reached more than 72,800 farmers, with 10,800 active users receiving tailored fertilizer advisories. Independent assessments show yield increases of 16–38% and profit gains of up to USD 669 per hectare, demonstrating its strong impact on smallholder productivity.

results.title: Knowledge and Data Sharing - Annual Technical Report 2024
results.description:
This report presents an overview of the strategic and technical contributions 
made by the Knowledge and Data Sharing team in 2024 to enhance 
information and results management within the AICCRA project. Central to 
these efforts was the continued development and optimization of the 
MARLO tool, which now plays a critical role in fostering a culture of 
monitoring, evaluation (M&E), and results-oriented project management. 
These updates have significantly improved the integrity, quality, and impact 
of research outputs.
The report highlights how improvements to MARLO and the implementation 
of the Data Management Plan—aligned with new funding streams and the 
revised results framework—have strengthened the project’s ability to 
deliver high-quality, verifiable results. By promoting open access principles 
and evidence-based approaches, the team has ensured that project 
outcomes are not only publicly available but also actionable, ultimately 
supporting more informed decision-making in the agricultural sector across 
Africa.
In summary, the report describes the main system improvements, progress 
in digital integration, and the skills development that took place within the 
Knowledge and Data Sharing team itself. These actions helped the team 
better support project staff with planning and reporting, allowing for more 
efficient and coordinated work across the AICCRA initiative.

results.title: RiceMoRe: Digitalizing Rice Monitoring for Climate Action and Scalable Impact
results.description: The Rice Activity Monitoring and Reporting System (RiceMoRe) is a digital solution co-created and implemented in Vietnam from 2018 to 2024 to address critical challenges in monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of rice activities, particularly concerning greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Previously, Vietnam lacked a digital system for tracking progress toward emission reduction targets, relying on manual, inconsistent, and often inaccurate reporting methods. This posed significant barriers to demonstrating climate mitigation achievements and accessing climate finance. RiceMoRe overcame this by digitizing the existing government reporting line, standardizing data entry, minimizing errors, and ensuring hierarchical quality controls. Developed on open-source platforms, it provides a low-cost, flexible, and replicable system. The primary outcome is the official adoption of RiceMoRe by Vietnam’s Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD), currently Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, scaling across approximately 75% of the country’s rice planting areas, significantly enhancing the efficiency, accuracy, transparency, traceability, and accessibility of agricultural data for climate action and sustainable rice management.

results.title: Development of an efficient seed dormancy breaking method for African rice (Oryza glaberrima)
results.description:
Seed dormancy is a significant factor limiting the conservation, evaluation, distribution and utilisation of African
cultivated rice, Oryza glaberrima. In this study, 20 accessions from the AfricaRice genebank were grown at
the AfricaRice Mbé station in Côte d’Ivoire, harvested manually, dried at 15% RH and 15°C, and stored at
-20°C for one month before use. Seeds underwent dry heat treatment at 50 or 60°C for 2, 4, 7, 14, 21 or 28
days, or were treated with: 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 M KCl; 0.022, 0.112, 0.224 or 0.448 M HNO3; 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4,
or 0.5 M KH2PO4; and 2.89, 5.77 or 14.44 mM gibberellic acid (GA3). Most treatments on intact seeds did not
significantly increase germination, except for those treated at 50°C for 21 or 28 days. Dehulled seeds germinated
effectively with all treatments except HNO3 solutions. After validating the treatment on 287 O. glaberrima
accessions, it was concluded that dry heat treatment at 50°C for 28 days effectively breaks dormancy. This
protocol improves germination percentages of O. glaberrima, enhancing its use in various studies and aiding
better decision-making in the management of O. glaberrima accessions in genebanks

results.description: This report assesses the outcomes of Zero Deforestation Agreements (ZDAs) in Colombia, voluntary and market-oriented public–private initiatives implemented since 2017 to reduce deforestation across key agricultural supply chains. It was elaborated under the CGIAR Climate Action Science Program. The analysis is situated in a post-conflict context characterized by accelerated deforestation driven by frontier expansion, land grabbing, and weak enforcement, which poses a challenging setting for voluntary sustainability initiatives. The study applies a mixed qualitative and institutional analysis grounded in a theory-of-change framework, drawing on stakeholder interviews, document review, and comparative sectoral analysis to examine governance, coordination, and behavioral outcomes of ZDAs in the beef and dairy and cocoa supply chains. Results show that in high-risk and fragmented sectors such as beef and dairy, ZDAs have had limited capacity to generate direct and measurable reductions in forest loss. Their main contributions have been institutional, including improved coordination, information sharing, learning processes, and emerging norms around deforestation-free production. However, weak traceability, misaligned incentives, and strong frontier dynamics continue to constrain their effectiveness. In contrast, in the cocoa sector, characterized by high organizational coverage and agroforestry-compatible production systems, ZDAs have been more effective in consolidating low-deforestation pathways, reinforcing sustainable production models, and facilitating alignment with emerging international due diligence and traceability requirements. The conclusions highlight that ZDAs function best as governance instruments embedded within broader environmental and agricultural policy frameworks rather than as stand-alone solutions. Their effectiveness depends on complementary regulatory baselines, credible economic incentives, and long-term financial commitments. When matched to sector-specific realities, ZDAs can either remain limited to pilot impacts or consolidate sustainable, deforestation-free production trajectories.

results.title: What satellites see vs what pastoralists know: A mapping story from the Karamoja Cluster
results.description: This carousel tells the story of how mapping for climate resilience and peace works best when satellite data is combined with local knowledge. Focusing on the Karamoja Cluster across Uganda, Kenya, South Sudan, and Ethiopia, it shows why understanding mobility, drought, and resource tension requires seeing beyond what remote sensing alone can capture. The carousel walks through a two-phase mapping process: first, large-scale remote mapping using satellite imagery and machine learning, and then participatory mapping with local communities to fill critical gaps. Pastoralists helped identify missing buildings, seasonal resources, and local realities invisible to satellites. The result is a richer, more accurate dataset that reflects how people actually live and move. The key message is that maps shape decisions about aid, services, and investment, and without grounding data in lived experience, even well-designed systems can fail

results.title: Seguimiento a las asociaciones y parcelas demostrativas: “Construcción de paz medioambiental para mejorar la nutrición y reducir las emisiones en Cauca y Putumayo”
results.description: Through field visits, participatory workshops, and continuous virtual support, the project monitored the establishment and management of biofortified bean plots, the preparation and application of bio-inputs, and the strengthening of local agronomic capacities. The activities involved five producer associations across Cauca and Putumayo and combined sustainable soil management practices, organic fertilization, post-harvest handling, and participatory evaluation of improved bean lines. The experience highlights the relevance of demonstration plots as learning spaces, the importance of farmer-led experimentation, and the role of low-emission agricultural practices in improving productivity, food and nutrition security, and territorial resilience in conflict-affected rural areas.

results.title: Perfil del proyecto: Fortalecer el sector ganadero mediante la construcción y dotación de una planta productora de sal mineralizada en San Vicente del Caguán
results.description:
En el marco del Grant GIZ–CIAT 81310949 y con aportes del Scaling for Impact Program del CGIAR, se desarrollaron nueve perfiles de proyectos orientados a impulsar modelos de ganadería sostenible y libre de deforestación en las cadenas láctea y cárnica. Asimismo, contó con aportes de los Acuerdos Cero Deforestación y con el apoyo del proyecto UK PACT – Transformando las cadenas de suministro hacia un futuro libre de deforestación, implementado por la Alianza de Bioversity International y el CIAT, así como con el respaldo de los contribuyentes al Fondo Fiduciario del CGIAR.

Estos perfiles ofrecen una hoja de ruta para la estructuración y gestión de proyectos de inversión pública y privada, dirigida a empresas del sector, el Ministerio de Agricultura, ONG y entidades firmantes de los Acuerdos Cero Deforestación. El proceso metodológico incluye: análisis de contexto y políticas, identificación de mecanismos de financiamiento bajo un enfoque de cadena de valor, definición de líneas de inversión en sostenibilidad y gestión de proyectos ante fuentes de financiamiento.

Los perfiles, elaborados en marco lógico, integran diagnóstico, alternativas de solución, objetivos, indicadores y estrategias de implementación, consolidándose en lineamientos técnicos y prácticos para fortalecer capacidades en la formulación de proyectos hacia una ganadería sostenible y libre de deforestación.

They also received contributions from the Zero Deforestation Agreements and support from the UK PACT project – Transforming supply chains toward a deforestation-free future, implemented by the Bioversity International and CIAT Alliance, as well as backing from contributors to the CGIAR Trust Fund.

These profiles provide a roadmap for structuring and managing public and private investment projects, directed to sector companies, the Ministry of Agriculture, NGOs and entities signatory to the Zero Deforestation Agreements. The methodological process includes: context and policy analysis, identification of financing mechanisms using a value-chain approach, definition of investment lines in sustainability and project management for financing sources.

The profiles, developed using a logical framework, integrate diagnosis, solution alternatives, objectives, indicators and implementation strategies, consolidating technical and practical guidelines to strengthen capacities in project formulation toward sustainable, deforestation-free livestock.

results.title: Resilient Seed System Development for Community Seed Banks in Western Kenya
results.description: Ensuring the availability of high-quality and healthy seeds, particularly the neglected and underutilized species (NUS) remains a critical challenge in effective agrobiodiversity conservation and utilization to enhance resilient nutritive food security. The formal seed sector largely concentrates on a limited number of crops, leaving gaps in farmers’ access to diverse and farmer-preferred resilient crop varieties. The national and international partners, namely the Alliance- Bioversity International & CIAT, the Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO) and the local county authorities devoted concerted efforts to support establishment and development of community seed banks in western Kenya. The International Center for Agriculture Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA) joined the program in 2023 under the CGIAR Nature Positive Solutions Initiative and continues under the Multifunctional landscape scientific program of the same. The ICARDA intervention focused on development of (1) a farmer-friendly variety catalogue, (2) early generation seed production manual, (3) provision of post-harvest seed operations equipment and facilities, and (4) the necessary capacity development to maximize the benefits from the facilities. The purpose of the Support to Resilient Seed System Development for Community Seed Banks in Western Kenya was to strengthen the functionality and sustainability of community seed banks in Kisumu and Vihiga Counties through capacity building, equipment upgrading, and demonstration of improved seed production and post-harvest practices. Specifically, the visit’s aim was to ensure effective utilization of post-harvest seed processing equipment, enhance the technical skills of CSB members, and support the implementation of demonstration activities that promote quality seed production and dissemination under the CGIAR Multifunctional Land Scape Science program building on the achievements of Nature Positive Solutions Initiative investments. This first Technical Support and Capacity Development under the MFL program was carried out from 26 to 29 August to kickstart the program’s follow-up process. The mission focused on (1) upgrading of post-harvest seed operation equipment provided under the N+ initiative, (2) training Community Seed Bank (CSB) members, and (3) designing and implementing demonstration activities on crop catalogue and EGS production manual enhancement. This report summarizes these activities.

results.title: Regional multi-stakeholder workshop organized by IRRI on potential pathways for methane mitigation in Southeast Asia’s rice sector held in the Philippines
results.description: The three‑day regional workshop held in Makati City, Philippines, marked the launch of IRRI’s AcceLER project, bringing together delegates from Cambodia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Viet Nam, with observers from Indonesia, Lao PDR, and Malaysia. The event centered on accelerating methane‑reducing rice practices across Southeast Asia. Workshop discussions highlighted the need for accessible and scalable climate‑smart practices, emphasized in opening remarks by Philippine Agriculture Undersecretary Christopher Morales. Participants worked on shaping national methane‑reduction roadmaps, targeting a 15% decrease in rice‑sector methane emissions by 2030. Sessions focused on strengthening Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) systems, including remote‑sensing tools, to improve data accuracy for national climate commitments. IRRI scientists underscored the importance of robust MRV and evidence‑based data for achieving NDC targets. The workshop also explored regulatory gaps, technologies influencing emissions, and opportunities for climate financing and carbon markets, fostering collaboration toward low‑emission rice production in the region.

results.title: Direct Seeders: Reducing Labor, Ensuring Timely Field Operations, and Mitigating End-of-Season Drought in Mali
results.description: Direct seeders are mechanized tools designed to plant rice seeds directly into prepared fields, bypassing traditional transplanting. This innovation reduces labor requirements, saves time, and ensures that field operations are completed promptly, which is critical for crop establishment. By enabling timely planting, direct seeders help mitigate the impacts of end-of-season droughts, improving crop survival and yields. They benefit smallholder farmers in Mali by enhancing efficiency, supporting sustainable production, and increasing resilience against climate-related stresses.

results.title: Leverage and expand successful extension experiences of established organizations in widespread on-farm variety demonstrations and marketing to increase farmers' access to improved varieties
results.description:
To increase farmers' access to improved varieties and support the seed and grain value chain actors to showcase benefits of new varieties; a total of 380 demonstration events were conducted (Tanzania: 47; Ethiopia: 333). In Ethiopia, these activities were supported by the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR) bean program and implemented in collaboration with multiple partners, including EIAR, EIAR/SAA, and the Hawassa and Jimma Agricultural Research Centers. The varieties promoted included SER119, Awash 3, Key Wolayita, Key Bure Miten, Tafash, and SER125. As a result a total of 83,342 (34,933 women) farmers have been reached. In Tanzania demo plots were established in collaboration with Farm Africa in Manyara region. Farmers were also linked to seed sources.
In Uganda, recently released biofortified and climate-resilient bean varieties, as well as non-varietal climate-smart innovations, were showcased during the World Food Day celebrations at Rwibitaba ZARDI.In Tanzania and Uganda, the demonstrations mainly focused on promoting newly released bean varieties.

results.title: A roadmap for solar irrigation expansion in Ethiopia
results.description: The project builds on five years of successful work in South Asia, where it proved that solar-powered irrigation helps farmers depend less on rainfall. The second phase of the project moves beyond irrigation to introduce a wide range of solar technologies such as cold storage, dryers, milling and agro-processing equipment that will help farmers lower production costs, keep their harvests fresh longer, reduce waste and create additional ways to earn an income. This holistic approach is designed to transform agricultural practices and improve the livelihoods of farmers.

results.title: Strategic advancement meetings conducted to evaluate promising crop varieties for farmers in West Africa
results.description: CGIAR's Accelerated Varietal Improvement and Seed Delivery of Legumes and Dryland Cereals in Africa initiative organized strategic meetings in Mali and Nigeria to evaluate the progress of new crop varieties through a systematic stage-gate process. These meetings brought together experts to assess groundnut, pearl millet, and sorghum varieties at critical decision points, determining which should advance to the next development phase based on performance data, farmer needs, and market potential. The disciplined evaluation process ensures that only the most promising varieties with proven benefits for climate resilience, nutrition, and poverty reduction continue through the breeding pipeline, optimizing resource allocation and increasing the likelihood that farmers will ultimately receive varieties that perform well under real world conditions in West Africa. The meeting involved invitation from a wide stakeholder team which included the product Design teams, where a number of key participants were invited. In the invitation gender balance was taken into considered to ensure balance.
